To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The heme domain of a direct oxygen sensor from Escherichian coli is coordinated by His-77 and Met-95, and the Met ligand is displaced by CO or O2.

the isolated heme domain of a direct oxygen sensor from Escherichian coli contains two axial heme ligands (His77 and Met95), and that the Met95 ligand is displaced by CO or O2 upon reduction of the heme.

the His77 and Met-95 mutants of the heme-bound PAS-domain (E. coli PAS) of a heme-containing oxygen sensor from E. coli were investigated with resonance raman spectroscopy, and that the heme environments of the His77 and the Met-95 mutants differ from that of the wild type enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the heme environment of the PAS domain of a direct oxygen sensor from E. coli, which is a model for a large number of oxygen sensors in bacteria.
the elucidation of the heme ligand environment and the mechanism of the heme redox reaction in the isolated heme domain of a direct oxygen sensor from E. coli. We
understanding the mechanism by which the E. coli DOS senses oxygen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Met95 is the ligand that is displaced from the heme upon reduction of the E. coli DOS heme domain.
the heme domain is not directly involved in sensing oxygen, but that the heme is a sensor for a ligand exchange that occurs in the protein following reduction of the heme.
the His77 residue is the proximal ligand of the heme in E. coli DOS and that the Met95 residue is a distal ligand of the reduced heme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heme domain of E. Coli DOS PAS has an oxygen-sensing function that is distinct from that of the heme domain in the
the heme domain of E. coll DOS PAS senses the redox state of the heme and the presence of O2 and CO.
E. coli DOS is an oxygen sensor that is activated upon binding of an unknown ligands to the heme of its PAS domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RR spectroscopic approach is a powerful tool for the characterization of heme-ligand interactions in PAS domain-containing proteins.
RR spectroscopy is an excellent tool for probing the heme environment of the PAS domain of the E. coli oxygen-sensor protein, DOS.

the heme environment of the PAS domain of E. colidos is very similar to that of the heme domain of a soluble heme-based oxygen sensor from Rhodobacter sphaeroides (R. sphaeroidesheme domain) and that both the heme domain and the PAS domain of R. sphaeroids DOS contain His and Met as axial ligands to the heme.
